t: A classroom project board for the Raspberry Pi Pico with dozens of built-in parts.
steps: Buy the EDU PICO kit from Cytron or a reseller such as PiShop South Africa.
Plug the Pico 2 W into the socket on the board.
Download the EDU PICO CircuitPython build from the CircuitPython website.
Hold the Pico button, connect USB, and drag the file onto the drive that appears.
Install the free Thonny or Mu editor on your computer.
Open the first guidebook lesson and blink the colored lights.
Move on to the temperature lesson and show the reading on the screen.
meta: Open Code. From $50.99. A few stores.
